subject.title: Concurrency: CloseWebSocketAsync skips _sendLock — a close racing an in-flight send throws and skips the graceful close

question: For a disconnect that races a send which never completes, should graceful close wait indefinitely for `_sendLock`, or should it use a bounded wait and then fall back to teardown?
rationale: The bug fix is narrow, but the timeout/fallback contract changes operator-visible disconnect behavior and cannot be selected safely from the current source report alone.

options.title: Use a bounded graceful-close wait
options.body: Wait briefly for an active send to drain, perform the close handshake when it does, then use the existing teardown path when it does not.

options.title: Always wait for the active send
options.body: Maximize graceful close completion, accepting that a stalled send may block disconnect indefinitely.

recommendation.title: Use a bounded graceful-close wait
recommendation.body: Wait briefly for an active send to drain, perform the close handshake when it does, then use the existing teardown path when it does not.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the detailed lifecycle analysis and a deterministic proposed reproduction, though current-main file ownership could not be established from the available history evidence.
